title: Exploiting Power Side-Channel Vulnerabilities in XGBoost Accelerator
problem: XGBoost accelerators on FPGAs are vulnerable to power side-channel attacks that can leak sensitive model data and enable model extraction.
motivation: Security of ML model parameters is critical for applications like ransomware and fraud detection; hardware-based vulnerabilities have not been fully explored.
method: Demonstrates power side-channel attacks by analyzing power consumption variations to infer XGBoost decision tree node features; uses empirical testing on Sakura-X platform with FAXID accelerator to deduce model decisions.
key_novelty: First comprehensive power side-channel attack on hardware-accelerated XGBoost demonstrating model parameter extraction via power consumption monitoring.
contributions: Comprehensive power side-channel vulnerability analysis of XGBoost FPGA accelerators
Method to infer node features and extract model decisions from power traces
Experimental demonstration on Sakura-X platform showing 367k tests sufficient for sensitive value leakage
High-accuracy fingerprinting (95.6%) of operations in real-world distributed systems

metrics.other: 367k tests to leak sensitive values, 95.6% fingerprint accuracy

primary_theme: power side-channel vulnerability in ML accelerators
